To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Upper Miocene of southern Spain was deposited in a ramp setting and that the facies distribution is the result of facies partitioning and a complex relief.
the Upper Miocene sediments of the Ronda basin can be divided into 3 sequences, and that the facies distribution is controlled by a combination of sequence stratigraphy and facies partitioning.
The Upper Miocene sediments in the Ronda Basin are divided into three deposi-tional sequences.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of sequence stratigraphy in a cool-water carbonate-siliciclatic system and the application of sequence stratigraphy to the development of depositional models for cool-water carbonate-sandstone successions.
the development of sequence stratigraphy and the application of this concept to cool-water carbonates and mixed carbonate-siliceclastic systems in a cool-water setting.
the facies and depositional environments of a cool-water carbonate system and with the influence of siliciclastic input.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Ronda Basin was flooded by a cool water body, which was influenced by the Atlantic Ocean and the Mediterranean Sea.
Sequence 1 is a lowstand systems tract, Sequence 2 a transgressive systems tract, and Sequence  3 a highstand systems tract.
Sequence 1 is characterized by conglomerates and Sequence 2 and 3 are dominated by carbonate sediments.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cool-water carbonates can be deposited under a wide range of environmental conditions.
the distribution of cool-water carbonate facies in the Ronda Basin is controlled by the distribution of siliciclastic sedi-ments, and by the relief of the underlying basement.
cool-water carbonate deposits are more abundant in the inner ramp than in the middle and/or outer ramp, and that bryomol and rhodalgal deposits occur under different environmental conditions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the facies partitioning of cool-water carbonates in mixed carbonate-siliclaticlastic ramp systems is strongly influenced by the morphology of the basin and the position in the ramp.
the cool-water carbonated sediments of the Guadalquivar Domain are not the product of a single factory.
cool-water carbonates are not necessarily associated with siliciclastical sediments.
